channel.title: The Librarian Abroad
channel.description: Notes from the road and from the table — what was worth the trip, what was worth the plate, and what wasn't.

item.title: A Good Burger and a Locked Gate, at Dick's Primal Kitchen
item.description: The kitchen here is doing something genuinely uncommon — 100% grass-fed and finished beef, a menu built to be taken apart and rebuilt. Then some time after nine they padlocked the back gate with my car still behind it, and that is why this entry has one star instead of four. (Portland, Oregon)

item.title: Fully Involved, at Firehouse Subs
item.description: A New York Steamer ordered "fully involved," a hot sauce bar named after the founders' own father, and the case for why a sandwich chain's branding can be this good and its app can still be this bad. (Vancouver, Washington)

item.title: The Egg Coffee at Trung Nguyên Legend
item.description: A tray, a bowl of hot water underneath to keep it warm, and a whipped egg-yolk foam dusted with cocoa — Vietnam's answer to tiramisu in a cup, plus a whole rotating board of specialty drinks worth its own second visit. (Portland, Oregon)

item.title: The Prosciutto and Brie Panini at St Honoré Boulangerie
item.description: A grilled panini of prosciutto and brie on the boulangerie's own baguette, eaten at a sidewalk table in downtown Lake Oswego — worth traveling across the city for, and I did. (Lake Oswego, Oregon)

item.title: Reading the Flavor Board at Salt & Straw
item.description: Third stop of the day, twenty minutes after lunch — and a case for why "adventurous" isn't automatically the same thing as "better," at least where ice cream is concerned. (Lake Oswego, Oregon)

item.title: The Sandy Sauce at Cactus Ya Ya
item.description: A steak yaya roll and a fried fish taco to close out a Sunday food crawl at a Vancouver institution I've been driving twenty-five minutes to for years — and a case for why the happy hour burger, with a little-known sauce most people never ask about, might be the better order. (Vancouver, Washington)

item.title: The Pink Lady at Artisserie Fine Bakery
item.description: A hand-sized dome of almond cake and mirror glaze, a few doors down from lunch — the kind of pastry that looks too good to cut into and tastes better than it looks. (Lake Oswego, Oregon)

item.title: The Chashu at Ramen Ryoma
item.description: Three slices of pork in a Hokkaido miso broth, in a strip-mall shop behind a Japanese grocery in Beaverton — and the best bowl of ramen I have eaten on this coast. (Beaverton, Oregon)

item.title: Opening the Kitchen
item.description: A first entry, and a plain statement of what this notebook is for — roads, tables, and the honest verdict on both. (Vancouver, Washington)

item.title: The Trick with the Peppers, at In-N-Out
item.description: A brand-new location on SE 3rd Way, a Double-Double taken apart and rebuilt with pickle brine and pepper juice, and an argument for why nothing else in fast food beats In-N-Out on the ratio that actually matters. (Vancouver, Washington)
